On your answers — all clear. For item 1, those three stop points are already what the candidate text encodes: the first two are the per-commit flow's Work-review and Description-review gates (stops five and seven), and the delegated-ladder case is exactly the new Scope bullet — intermediate pushes are steps, the hard stop lands at close-out. So I don't think the final text needs anything added beyond possibly one sentence noting that the in-conversation gates are the review of record and `vc-x1 push`'s interactive gates are redundant when they've already run. We can settle that wording when we adopt.

On **moving `notes/todo.md` → `./TODO.md`**: I'm for it. The entry's own argument is the strongest one — it's the same "easy for everyone to find beats convenient" principle that put AGENTS.md at the root, applied consistently. The todo list is the project's live state and the single most-read file (the routine acquaint read); root-level uppercase puts it where both a human browsing GitHub and a bot listing the project root see it without being told. `TODO.md` at root is also a real, recognized convention, so it costs no surprise. And the "entry point at root, siblings stay in `notes/`" shape is exactly the README→docs/ pattern — the asymmetry is a feature, not an inconsistency.

Two costs worth having eyes-open about, one of which the entry doesn't name:

- **The named one-time churn** (relative links gain `notes/` prefixes, inbound links, src/ help-text sweep) — mechanical and bounded, agreed.
- **A small *ongoing* tax the entry doesn't mention**: the retire-Done flow. Migrating a Done entry from `TODO.md` to `notes/done.md` currently moves refs between two files in the *same* directory, so `[N]:` definition paths copy verbatim. After the move they cross directories — a ref written `notes/bugs.md#...` in TODO.md must become `bugs.md#...` when its entry lands in done.md. Every migration beat pays a path-adjustment step forever. It's small and mechanical, but it's the one recurring cost, and worth a line in the Retiring-Done mechanics (or a future `fix-todo`/`validate-repo` check) so it doesn't become a drip of dangling refs.

I also agree with both sub-decisions recorded in the entry: **sequencing after this sync round lands** (it touches the shared AGENTS.md File-reads section, so stacking it into the current round would muddy two logically distinct changes to the same shared text), and **hard paths in the shared AGENTS.md** — greppability is the working currency of this whole convention set; naming the file abstractly ("the todo file") would break the grep-first workflow to dodge a churn cost you only pay once per rare rename.

One tiny addition for when it lands: the File-reads bullet should keep TODO.md first as the acquaint read, and the `vc-x1 fix-todo` / `validate-todo` examples in the shared text will want their example path updated (`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md`) — the tools take the path as an argument, so it's docs-only, consistent with the entry's "code behavior unaffected" note.

77	A chores section's `Commits:` line cites the commit(s) it

# Build a 4-revision substep ladder for manual squash inspection.

# State after this script:

set -euo pipefail

ROOT=/tmp/substep-test

rm -rf "$ROOT"
mkdir -p "$ROOT"
cd "$ROOT"

jj git init --colocate >/dev/null

content.text:
Ready to commit indeed — the shared set is in its final round shape.

On `notes/substep-test.sh` — what it is: a scratch harness that builds a throwaway 4-revision jj ladder under `/tmp/substep-test` so the squash recipes can be exercised by hand. It's the tool that validated the "Close-out: squash the ladder" recipes now in cycle-protocol.md — that work is recorded in *vc-x1's* chores-07, which cites the script by path.

**Does it have future use?** Modest but real: it's the fastest way to re-validate the squash/`--ignore-immutable` recipes when a jj upgrade changes semantics, or if someone reworks the sub-cycle ladder section. But it's ~50 frozen lines, trivially reconstructible from its own header comment, and its story belongs to vc-x1's history, not the template's — here it's inherited seed content with no chores section of its own.

**So: agree with removing it from the template** (it's already deleted in this working copy). On how to preserve it, two defensible shapes:

- **Your code-block idea** — paste it into a `###` subsection of the current chores-NN.md here. In its favor: grep-findable in a checkout and immediately copy-paste runnable. The usual objection to duplicating artifacts into chores — two copies drift — doesn't apply to a deleted file; the embed becomes the only checkout copy, frozen.
- **The convention-purist alternative** — a one-line chores bullet: removed `notes/substep-test.sh` (jj squash-ladder scratch harness; validated the sub-cycle squash recipes — see vc-x1 chores-07), recoverable via `git show <removing-sha>^:notes/substep-test.sh`. The `Commits:` backfill supplies the SHA one push later. This is the "git is the record" answer: the artifact stays in history, the chores line makes "substep-test" greppable, and chores files don't start collecting attachments.

My lean is the **one-line bullet + history pointer**, mainly for the precedent: once one script gets embedded, chores files become the attic, and the project's own principle is that git owns mechanical content while chores owns narrative. The two-step recovery (`git log --grep`, then `git show`) is a fair price for that. But if you weight immediate usability higher, the embed is legitimate here precisely because the file is small, frozen, and self-contained — I'd just make it the exception, not the pattern.

One side note either way: this is a template-only decision. vc-x1's chores-07 actively references `notes/substep-test.sh` as a live path, so vc-x1 should keep its copy (or make its own embed decision in its own story) — otherwise those references dangle over there.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and
surfaced, and how often it changes — pick the case that fits
your medium:

- **Manifest** — where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the
    committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic
    `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, …) — add the case as
    needed
- **Notation** — how the `-` form is stored:
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`),
    store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python
    project), remap to `+` — `0.3.0-5.3.0` → `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same
    version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter** — how a built artifact surfaces the
  version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence** — how often to bump: see
  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement);
  this project follows the per-commit preference.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change
on **every commit**, so a built or running artifact identifies
the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project
  following the cycle protocol may bump less often — once per

content.content:
vc-x1 0.69.0

Commit both repos, push the work repo's BOOKMARK, and
squash-push the bot repo's `main` — one resumable command.

Collapses the manual commit-push-publish ceremony into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates and a
state machine with persistent progress so interruptions can
resume without re-doing completed stages.

Stages: preflight (tracking / bot-published / sync checks —
no build steps; run project checks yourself before pushing)
→ review (approve diff)
→ message ($EDITOR / --title+--body, approve text) →
commit-work → commit-bot (skipped if clean) → bookmark-set
(work repo → <bookmark>, bot repo → main) → push-work →
squash-push-bot. Failures in commit-work / commit-bot /
bookmark-set roll both repos back via
`jj op restore` to the snapshot recorded before commit-work.
After push-work succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and
recovery is forward-only.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip the review gate. Saved state carries title/body
across resumes so only the first invocation needs them.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (positional form of
          `--bookmark`). The bot repo always advances `main`.
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (flag form; see positional)

  -V, --version
          Print the `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as the first line, then continue. With
          no subcommand, prints the banner and exits.
          
          Replaces clap's auto-version (which would exit after printing): the
          banner now rides along with normal subcommand execution rather than
          gating it, so scripts can capture the version *and* the command's
          output in one invocation.

      --restart
          Clear any saved state file and start from stage 1

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --from <STAGE>
          Explicit stage to jump to (advanced / debug use)

          Possible values:
          - preflight:       Verify bookmark tracking, the bot-published
            invariant, and sync state
          - review:          Present diff for the first approval gate
          - message:         Compose / edit the commit message; present for
            second gate
          - commit-work:     Commit the work repo
          - commit-bot:      Commit the `.claude` bot repo (skipped if empty)
          - bookmark-set:    Advance each repo's bookmark to its `@-`: work →
            `<bookmark>`, bot → `main`
          - push-work:       `jj git push --bookmark <b> -R .`
          - squash-push-bot: In-process squash of `.claude`'s trailing session
            writes + push `main`

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --status
          Print where the saved state thinks we are and exit

      --recheck
          Re-run `preflight` even on resume (default: skip if last run
          succeeded)

      --no-squash-push
          Stop before `squash-push-bot` so it can be run manually

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

      --title <STR>
          Commit title (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

      --body <STR>
          Commit body (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

  -y, --yes
          Auto-approve interactive prompts (review gate, message-edit
          confirmation). Required when `--title` / `--body` aren't both supplied
          in non-interactive contexts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
